# Lift Device Leveling System

## Overview

The lift device is built around a central chassis that serves as the primary structural framework for the leveling system. To enable comprehensive positional control, the device incorporates two distinct leveling assemblies: a rear leveling assembly coupled to the rear end of the chassis, and a front leveling assembly coupled to the front end of the chassis. Together, these assemblies work in coordination to maintain proper orientation and stability of the lift device across varying operating conditions.

## Rear Leveling Assembly

The rear leveling assembly is equipped with two actuators: a first rear actuator and a second rear actuator. These components are selectively engageable, allowing the system to actively manage the orientation of the rear end of the device. Through the controlled operation of these actuators, the assembly enables active control of both rear pitch and roll adjustments, ensuring that the rear of the lift device can be precisely positioned as required.

## Front Leveling Assembly

The front leveling assembly likewise contains two actuators: a first front actuator and a second front actuator. A key feature of these front actuators is their dual functionality, which is determined by their coupling state. Depending on how the actuators are configured, the front leveling assembly can operate in one of two distinct modes.

### Passive Control Mode

When the front actuators are selectively fluidly coupled, they facilitate passive control of the front pitch and roll adjustments. In this configuration, the interconnected actuators allow the front of the device to respond and adapt to changing conditions without requiring direct active intervention.

### Active Control Mode

Conversely, when the front actuators are selectively fluidly decoupled, they facilitate active control of the front pitch and roll adjustments. In this mode, the independently operating actuators enable precise, directed management of the front orientation, giving the system full control over the positioning of the front end of the lift device.

## Summary

By combining a rear leveling assembly capable of active pitch and roll control with a front leveling assembly that can alternate between passive and active control modes, the lift device achieves a versatile and adaptable leveling system. This design allows the device to maintain optimal stability and orientation across a wide range of operating scenarios.

# Lift Device with Adaptive Leveling System

## Overview

A lift device is described that incorporates an advanced leveling system designed to maintain a stable and level platform across a wide range of operating conditions and terrain types. The device is built around a central chassis that serves as the structural foundation for the lift mechanism and supports the various leveling assemblies. By combining active and passive control strategies, the system delivers precise orientation adjustments while balancing performance, complexity, and cost.

## Chassis and Structural Configuration

At the core of the device is a chassis that provides the primary support framework. The chassis is configured to carry the load-bearing components of the lift, including the elevating structure, and to interface with the ground-engaging elements that support the machine. Mounted to this chassis are two distinct leveling assemblies—one positioned toward the rear and one positioned toward the front—each responsible for controlling the orientation of the device along its pitch and roll axes.

## Rear Leveling Assembly

The rear portion of the chassis is equipped with a rear leveling assembly that employs a pair of independently controllable actuators, referred to as the first rear actuator and the second rear actuator. These actuators are selectively engageable, meaning that they can be individually commanded to extend or retract as required by the leveling logic.

Because the two rear actuators can be operated independently, the assembly is capable of **active pitch and roll control** at the rear of the machine. Adjusting both rear actuators together in the same direction alters the fore-aft attitude of the chassis, thereby controlling pitch. Adjusting the two rear actuators differentially—extending one while retracting or holding the other—produces a side-to-side tilt that controls roll. This dual capability allows the rear of the device to be actively driven to a desired orientation regardless of the underlying ground surface.

## Front Leveling Assembly

The front portion of the chassis is served by a front leveling assembly that likewise includes two actuators: a first front actuator and a second front actuator. What distinguishes the front assembly is its ability to operate in two selectable modes, giving the device its characteristic flexibility.

**Passive Mode (Fluidly Coupled):** In this mode, the first and second front actuators are selectively fluidly coupled to one another. When the actuators share a common fluid path, fluid can transfer freely between them in response to terrain-induced loads. As one front actuator is compressed by a rise in the ground, fluid is displaced into the opposing actuator, allowing it to extend correspondingly. This automatic fluid exchange enables the front of the chassis to conform to uneven ground without requiring dedicated control inputs, providing **passive front pitch and roll compensation**. This mode is well suited to situations where continuous, self-adjusting compliance is desirable and where active correction of the front is unnecessary.

**Active Mode (Decoupled):** Alternatively, the two front actuators can be fluidly decoupled from one another. Once isolated, each front actuator can be controlled independently, in a manner analogous to the rear actuators. In this configuration the front assembly provides **active pitch and roll control**, enabling the front of the chassis to be deliberately driven to a commanded orientation rather than simply reacting to ground contours.

## Flexible Leveling Capabilities

The combination of a fully active rear assembly with a selectively active or passive front assembly gives the lift device a versatile and adaptable leveling strategy. The operator, or an automated control system, can choose the appropriate mode based on the demands of the task and the nature of the terrain. Passive front control offers smooth, responsive compliance that reduces control complexity, while active front control offers precise, deliberate positioning when maximum stability and level accuracy are required.

## Benefits

By offering these selectable leveling behaviors, the described device significantly enhances both **stability** and **adaptability**. It can maintain a level working platform across varying and challenging terrain, improve safety during elevated operations, and reduce the risk of tipping or uneven load distribution. The flexibility to switch between active and passive front control ensures that the device can be optimized for a broad spectrum of operating scenarios, making it a robust and versatile solution for applications that demand reliable leveling performance.

# Patent Abstract

## Lift Device with Active and Passive Leveling Assemblies for Pitch and Roll Adjustment Control

A lift device is disclosed that includes a base, an elevatable platform, and front and rear leveling assemblies configured to provide both active and passive pitch and roll adjustment control. The front leveling assembly and the rear leveling assembly are operatively coupled between the base and the platform to selectively adjust the orientation of the platform relative to a ground surface. Each leveling assembly includes one or more actuators configured to provide active adjustment of the platform along a pitch axis and a roll axis in response to control signals, thereby maintaining the platform in a substantially level orientation during operation on uneven or sloped terrain.

The lift device further includes a control system in communication with the front and rear leveling assemblies and one or more sensors configured to detect an orientation of the platform. The control system is configured to command active pitch and roll adjustments based on sensor feedback to compensate for changes in terrain, load distribution, or device movement. The leveling assemblies are additionally configured to provide passive pitch and roll compliance, allowing the platform to accommodate transient forces and surface irregularities without active intervention, thereby enhancing stability and operator safety. The combination of active and passive leveling control enables improved platform stabilization, reduced structural loading, and enhanced operational performance across a range of working conditions.

# Lift Device Leveling Mechanism Summary

A lift device leveling system typically maintains a stable, level platform through coordinated operation of front and rear leveling assemblies. Here's a general overview of how such mechanisms work:

## Core Components

**Chassis**
- Serves as the structural foundation
- Provides mounting points for both leveling assemblies
- Distributes loads across the device

**Rear Leveling Assembly**
- Contains actuator(s) positioned at the rear of the device
- Compensates for terrain variations affecting the back of the platform

**Front Leveling Assembly**
- Contains multiple actuators at the front
- Manages front-end elevation and tilt corrections

## How Leveling Works

1. **Sensing** – Level sensors (inclinometers, tilt sensors, or position feedback devices) detect the platform's orientation relative to horizontal.

2. **Actuator Coordination** – The multiple actuators extend or retract independently or in coordinated fashion to:
   - Adjust height at different corners/points
   - Compensate for uneven ground
   - Correct pitch (front-to-back tilt) and roll (side-to-side tilt)

3. **Feedback Control** – A control system continuously compares actual orientation against a level reference and drives actuators to minimize error.

## Points to Clarify

To give you a more precise summary, it would help to know:

- **What specific device** is this? (scissor lift, aerial work platform, vehicle lift, wheelchair lift, etc.)
- Are you referencing a **particular patent or technical document**?
- Are the actuators **hydraulic, pneumatic, or electric**?

If you can share the source material or more details, I can tailor the summary to match the exact mechanism you're describing.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description of a lift device's leveling assemblies, explaining how the actuators enable pitch and roll adjustments.
counterfactuals.output:
# Lift Device Leveling Assemblies: Technical Description

## Overview

The leveling assembly is a critical subsystem responsible for maintaining a stable, level platform orientation regardless of terrain irregularities or load distribution. The system achieves precise angular correction through a coordinated arrangement of linear actuators, sensors, and a control module that governs pitch and roll adjustments in real time.

## System Architecture

The leveling assembly typically consists of the following primary components:

- **Linear Actuators** — Electromechanical or hydraulic devices that provide the extension/retraction force for platform correction
- **Inclinometer/IMU Sensors** — Dual-axis tilt sensors that continuously measure angular deviation
- **Control Module** — A processor that interprets sensor data and commands actuator response
- **Mounting Frame and Pivots** — Structural interfaces that transfer actuator motion into platform articulation

## Actuator Configuration

To achieve two-axis leveling, the system employs a **minimum of three or four actuators** arranged at the corners or along the orthogonal axes of the platform base. Each actuator operates independently under closed-loop control, allowing differential extension across the mounting points.

### Common Layouts

| Configuration | Actuator Count | Correction Capability |
|--------------|----------------|----------------------|
| Tripod | 3 | Full pitch and roll via triangulated geometry |
| Four-corner | 4 | Redundant, high-stability correction |
| Dual-axis gimbal | 2 | Independent pitch and roll on gimbaled mount |

## Pitch Adjustment (Fore-Aft Axis)

Pitch describes rotation about the **lateral (side-to-side) axis**, tilting the platform forward or backward.

To correct pitch:

1. The inclinometer detects a fore-aft angular deviation exceeding the tolerance threshold.
2. The control module calculates the required differential displacement.
3. **Front-mounted actuators extend while rear actuators retract** (or vice versa), creating a longitudinal height differential.
4. This differential rotates the platform about its lateral pivot until the sensor reads zero deviation.

## Roll Adjustment (Lateral Axis)

Roll describes rotation about the **longitudinal (fore-aft) axis**, tilting the platform left or right.

To correct roll:

1. The sensor detects a lateral tilt.
2. The controller commands the **left-side actuators to extend while right-side actuators retract** (or the reverse).
3. The resulting side-to-side height differential rotates the platform about its longitudinal axis until level.

## Combined Motion and Coordinated Control

Because pitch and roll corrections often occur simultaneously, the control module resolves both angular errors into a **combined displacement command for each actuator**. Each actuator's target position is the vector sum of its required pitch contribution and roll contribution. This coordinated actuation allows the platform to correct compound tilt in a single, smooth motion.

The system operates as a **closed feedback loop**:

```
Sensor Reading → Error Calculation → Actuator Command → 
Platform Correction → Updated Sensor Reading → (repeat)
```

## Operational Considerations

- **Range of Correction** — Limited by maximum actuator stroke length; typically ±5° to ±15°.
- **Response Rate** — Governed by actuator velocity and control loop update frequency.
- **Load Holding** — Self-locking mechanical actuators (e.g., ball or lead screws) maintain position without continuous power draw.
- **Safety Interlocks** — The system inhibits elevation functions until level status is confirmed, preventing unstable operation at height.

## Summary

The leveling assembly translates independent linear actuator motion into precise angular platform control. By extending and retracting actuators differentially—longitudinally for pitch and laterally for roll—the system maintains a level work surface under varying terrain and load conditions, with continuous sensor feedback ensuring accuracy and stability throughout operation.

counterfactuals.output:
# Abstract

A vehicle lift system and method for supporting a vehicle at a desired elevation while maintaining a level platform orientation. The system includes a plurality of actuators configured to raise and lower a load-supporting structure. The actuators are operable in a plurality of selectable modes to achieve leveling of the supported load. In an active leveling mode, a controller selectively engages one or more of the actuators independently based on feedback from one or more sensors indicative of platform orientation, thereby adjusting the relative extension of individual actuators to correct for misalignment or uneven loading. In a passive leveling mode, two or more of the actuators are selectively coupled in fluid communication with one another, permitting hydraulic fluid to transfer between the coupled actuators such that the actuators self-equalize in response to load distribution without active control intervention. A valve arrangement enables selective fluid coupling and decoupling of the actuators to transition between the active and passive leveling modes. The system thereby provides responsive, controlled leveling under dynamic conditions while enabling energy-efficient, self-balancing support under static or steady-state conditions.
